CONSENT TO TELEHEALTH SERVICES

Cascade Valley Behavioral Health, PLLC
1330 North Washington Street, Suite 210
Spokane, Washington 99201

Patient name: ____________________________    Date of birth: ______________

Please read this form carefully. Ask us any question you have before you sign it.

1. What telehealth is.

Telehealth means we deliver health care to you using live video, audio, or secure messaging instead of an in-person visit. Your provider may be in a different location than you are. Telehealth may include the exchange of your medical records, images, and other information between your provider and other health care professionals involved in your care.

2. Your rights.

Your participation is voluntary. You may refuse telehealth at any time and ask for an in-person appointment instead, and refusing will not affect your right to future care, your benefits, or the quality of care you receive. You may withdraw this consent at any time by telling your provider or by writing to us at the address above. You may ask that anyone not necessary to your care leave the room during a telehealth visit.

3. Benefits and risks.

The benefits of telehealth may include better access to care, shorter waits, and fewer trips. The risks may include: the video or audio quality may be poor enough that your provider cannot make a full assessment; technology may fail before or during the visit; your provider may not be able to perform a physical examination; delays in evaluation may occur; and, despite our safeguards, a transmission could be intercepted or your information could be disclosed to someone not authorized to see it.

4. Privacy and security.

We use a HIPAA-compliant telehealth platform with encryption in transit and at rest. We do not record telehealth visits, and nobody may record a visit without the written consent of everyone taking part. Your telehealth visits are documented in your medical record and are protected by the same federal and Washington laws that protect an in-person visit, including the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 and Chapter 70.02 RCW. Our Notice of Privacy Practices describes how we use and disclose your health information.

5. Where you and your provider must be.

Your provider is licensed to practice in Washington. Under Washington law, your provider may treat you by telehealth only when you are physically located in a state where the provider is licensed. Tell your provider at the start of every visit where you are physically located that day. If you are outside Washington, we may have to reschedule or refer you.

6. Emergencies.

Telehealth is not for emergencies. If you are having a medical emergency, or are thinking about harming yourself or someone else, call 911 or go to the nearest emergency department. You may also call or text 988 for the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline. At the start of each visit your provider will confirm your location and an emergency contact so that help can be sent if it is needed.

7. If technology fails.

If the connection drops and cannot be restored within five minutes, your provider will call you at the phone number on file to finish the visit by telephone or to reschedule. Give your provider a working phone number at the start of every visit.

8. Cost.

Telehealth visits are billed the same way in-person visits are. Your insurer may cover telehealth differently than an in-person visit, and you are responsible for any copayment, coinsurance, deductible, or non-covered charge. We will give you a good faith estimate before a scheduled visit if you are uninsured or choose not to use insurance, as required by the No Surprises Act.

9. Follow-up and records.

You may ask for a copy of your medical record, including the documentation of any telehealth visit, in the manner described in our Notice of Privacy Practices. Your provider will tell you how to reach the practice between visits and how quickly to expect a response.

10. Acknowledgment.

By signing below I confirm that: I have read this form, or it has been read to me; I have had the chance to ask questions and my questions were answered; I understand the benefits and risks described above; and I consent to receive health care by telehealth. I understand that I may withdraw this consent at any time.
